real_world_evidence: Most acute headaches in primary care are tension or migraine related
Red flags include neurologic deficits, thunderclap onset, fever, and age >50 with new headache
medical_issues: Check blood pressure and neurologic exam
Rule out secondary causes when red flags are present
guidelines: Use a headache red-flag framework before symptomatic treatment
Avoid unnecessary imaging when no neurologic warning signs

real_world_evidence: In ambulatory care, most fevers are viral and self-limited
Duration, localizing symptoms, and host risk factors improve triage
medical_issues: Assess for sepsis criteria and immunocompromise
Confirm hydration status and hemodynamic stability
guidelines: Escalate care when systemic instability or persistent high fever is present
Use local infectious disease guidance for testing

real_world_evidence: Acute cough is commonly viral and resolves within 3 weeks
Smoking history and chronicity help stratify risk
medical_issues: Screen for hypoxia, dyspnea, and hemoptysis
Review asthma/COPD history and inhaler use
guidelines: Avoid routine antibiotics in uncomplicated viral cough
Use chest imaging when pneumonia is suspected

real_world_evidence: Dyspnea is a high-risk symptom requiring prompt severity assessment
Pulse oximetry and work of breathing correlate with deterioration risk
medical_issues: Evaluate oxygenation, airway, and circulation first
Consider pulmonary embolism, heart failure, asthma/COPD, and infection
guidelines: Immediate escalation for severe distress or low oxygen saturation

real_world_evidence: Chest pain requires urgent exclusion of acute coronary syndrome
Risk stratification tools improve disposition safety
medical_issues: Consider pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal differentials
guidelines: Emergency pathway when ACS cannot be ruled out

real_world_evidence: Use complete history and examination to contextualize symptoms
medical_issues: Check for red flags and drug contraindications
guidelines: Follow local and specialty society guidance
